pages.title: Collections
pages.content:
Collections

What we take, and the rounds we run.

Shoko Archives collects business paper from your office on Tuesday and Thursday, boxes it, and barcodes it before the van leaves the dock. The store is Unit 7 at Harlow Mead Trading Estate in Lindenport.

What we take

A collection is for paper you have finished with in the office and still need to keep. We take invoices and ledgers, HR files, contracts, project drawings, legal holds, and closed-year boxes. A six-partner law office keeps 220 boxes of closed matters with us.

A family clinic keeps 90 boxes against a retention schedule. An architects' studio keeps 140 boxes of drawings and asks for a scan when a sheet is needed. Tomas Lindqvist drives the collection rounds.

At the dock, barcodes are checked on a clipboard before the boxes move to a numbered aisle. If your files match one of those six kinds of paper, they can go on the next Tuesday or Thursday round.

Invoices & ledgers Closed-year accounts, boxed by year.

HR files Personnel records kept on a schedule.

Contracts Signed agreements, past their working life.

Project drawings Rolled or folded to fit the box.

Legal holds Stay sealed until you say the hold has ended.

Closed-year boxes Anything the office no longer opens.

What we do not take

We take business paper in a standard archive box, and we leave the rest. Loose sheets are not a standing load; they are boxed and barcoded first. We do not store stock, equipment, furniture, or personal belongings.

We do not run a public reading room, and we do not take walk-in deposits on a Saturday morning. Saturday, 08:00–12:00, is for retrievals only. A legal hold stays sealed until you tell us it has ended.

We do not destroy a box on our own account. Secure destruction happens only when you request it, at €2.20 per box, and you receive a certificate. Daily working files stay at your desk.

Closed-year boxes are the ones that belong on the round.

The standard box

There is one box size: the standard archive box, supplied with a barcode at €3.50 each, excluding VAT. A collection visit covers up to 40 boxes and costs €45 per visit. Larger moves are booked as 41–120 or 120+ on the booking form, and they are split across Tuesday and Thursday rounds rather than treated as one visit.

The law office's 220 boxes and the studio's 140 boxes of drawings were collected that way. Once a box is indexed, storage is €0.42 per box per month. Invoices, ledgers, HR files, and contracts use the same box.

Project drawings go in it when they are rolled or folded to fit. The barcode applied at your office is the one we scan when the box is shelved.

Tuesday and Thursday rounds

Pickup rounds run on Tuesday and Thursday. The next pickup round is Tuesday. Hours at Unit 7 are Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00.

Saturday is 08:00–12:00 and is limited to retrievals. The store is closed on Sunday. Book a collection by phone on +00 20 7000 1404 or by email at hello@shoko-archives.example, or send the booking form with your name, company, a box-count band, and the round you prefer.

Priya Raman looks after client accounts and will match the visit to a round. After the boxes are collected they are indexed with an aisle, bay, and shelf address, then requested later by box number. A standard return is on your desk the next working day.

Book a collection

pages.title: Indexing & Retrieval
pages.content:
Indexing & Retrieval

A barcode, an address and a box number.

Every box receives a barcode and an aisle, bay, and shelf address before it is shelved. You ask for it by box number, and a standard return is the next working day.

From barcode to desk

Barcode and address

Jonah Whitfield leads indexing. When a box arrives from a Tuesday or Thursday collection, the barcode label is checked and the box is given an address: aisle, bay, and shelf. The building has 14 aisles, numbered 1–14, in Unit 7 at Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport. Capacity is 38,000 standard boxes. Elena Sousa supervises the aisles and the place each box occupies on the shelf. The address stays with the box for as long as you store it. You do not need a description of the contents to get the box back. The box number on the barcode is the reference we both use. Storage while it sits at that address is €0.42 per box per month, excluding VAT.

Request by box number

You request a box by its box number. A standard retrieval is the next working day and costs €6 per box. An urgent retrieval is the same day if you request it before 11:00, and it costs €18 per box. Requests that come in after 11:00 follow the next working day. Saturday hours are 08:00–12:00 and are for retrievals only. The desk is closed on Sunday. Weekday hours are Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00. Call +00 20 7000 1404 or email hello@shoko-archives.example and quote the box number. The returned box is the same standard archive box that left your office. Priya Raman can confirm which boxes sit on your account if you have more than one number to hand.

Scan on demand

Kenji Abara runs the scanning desk. If you need a page and not the whole box, ask for a scan on demand. The document is read at the desk, and the box goes back to its aisle, bay, and shelf. The architects' studio, with 140 boxes of drawings, uses this when a single sheet is required. A scan does not replace a retrieval: if you need the paper itself, we retrieve the box. Next-day return still applies to a physical box at €6, or the same day at €18 when the request is in before 11:00. The box number remains the way you call the file. The original is not sent out of Unit 7 unless you ask for the box.

Next-day return

The path is the one we publish: book, collect on Tuesday or Thursday, index with a barcode and an aisle–bay–shelf address, shelve, request by box number, and return the next working day. A collection visit is €45 for up to 40 boxes. The standard box with barcode is €3.50. When a holding period you have set comes to an end, secure destruction with a certificate is €2.20 per box, and only on your request. Legal holds are not destroyed while you still mark them as holds. Invoices, ledgers, HR files, contracts, project drawings, and closed-year boxes all use this same index. There is no separate code for each kind of paper.

pages.title: Prices
pages.content:
Prices

Six prices, in EUR, excluding VAT.

Prices are in euros and exclude VAT. Invoicing is monthly. The six lines below are the full price list for collection, boxes, storage, retrieval, and destruction.

The price list

All prices in EUR, excluding VAT. Invoiced monthly.

What each line covers

The collection visit is one stop for up to 40 boxes on a Tuesday or Thursday round, at €45. If you have 41–120 boxes, or 120+, say so on the booking form so the work can be split across rounds. The law office's 220 boxes, the clinic's 90 boxes, and the studio's 140 boxes of drawings are all stored as standard boxes under this list.

The barcode belongs to the box line, at €3.50 each. Storage at €0.42 per box per month is the holding charge across the 14 aisles. Retrieval by box number is either €6 the next working day or €18 the same day before 11:00.

Scan on demand is arranged with the scanning desk. This list does not state a separate figure for a scan.

Monthly invoicing

Invoicing is monthly. Storage for the boxes held that month, at €0.42 per box, appears on the monthly invoice, together with any collection visits, boxes supplied, retrievals, and destruction you asked for in that month. We do not add a charge that is not on the six-line list.

Prices are in euros and exclude VAT. Priya Raman handles client accounts from Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport. Questions on an invoice go to hello@shoko-archives.example or +00 20 7000 1404 during Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00.

Saturday, 08:00–12:00, is for retrievals only, and the store is closed on Sunday. The next pickup round is Tuesday.

Book a collection

pages.title: Our Facility
pages.content:
Our Facility

Unit 7, since 2004.

Shoko Archives has kept business paper at Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport, since 2004. The store is 14 aisles, with room for 38,000 standard boxes.

Since 2004

Mara Okonkwo founded Shoko Archives in 2004 and still runs operations from Unit 7. The work has stayed the same: collect paper on a round, barcode the box, put it in a numbered aisle, and bring it back when you ask. The address is Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport.

The phone is +00 20 7000 1404 and the email is hello@shoko-archives.example. Weekday hours are Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00. Saturday is 08:00–12:00 for retrievals only.

On Sunday the unit is closed. Pickup rounds are Tuesday and Thursday, and the next pickup round is Tuesday. Hall Two, a second hall, is on a waitlist and opens in spring.

Boxes we hold today stay in the 14 aisles of Unit 7.

Aisles, climate, and fire

The facility is 14 aisles, Aisle 1–14, with a capacity of 38,000 standard boxes. Elena Sousa supervises the aisles. Each box has an aisle, bay, and shelf address set at indexing under Jonah Whitfield.

The unit is run as a paper store: the aisles are kept dry and even so closed-year boxes, contracts, and drawings stay in readable condition. Fire protection is part of the building, so a box remains in its place on the shelf. We describe the store by its address and its capacity, not by a degree setting or a rating code.

What you can check is the barcode and the aisle–bay–shelf address. A standard retrieval from these aisles is the next working day. An urgent retrieval is the same day if you request it before 11:00.

14 aisles Aisle 1–14, steel shelving.

38,000 boxes Capacity in standard archive boxes.

Dry, even aisles Closed-year boxes stay readable.

Fire protection Built into the unit; boxes stay in place.

Controlled access No public counter; staff pull the box.

Access

Access to the aisles is controlled. The store is not a public counter, and boxes are not browsed by visitors. Your team requests a box by number, and staff pull it. Kenji Abara's scanning desk handles scan on demand inside the unit, so a page can be read without sending the box out. Tomas Lindqvist's collections use the loading dock on Tuesday and Thursday. People who come for a retrieval do so in the published hours. Saturday morning retrievals run from 08:00 to 12:00. If you need to speak to someone about access for a large collection, call +00 20 7000 1404 in weekday hours, Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00. Client accounts sit with Priya Raman.

pages.title: People
pages.content:
People

Six people, reached by name.

Six people handle the boxes, from the collection round to the scanning desk. Each one has a named duty on the path from your office to the aisle and back.

Who handles your boxes

Mara Okonkwo Founder, operations

Tomas Lindqvist Driver, collection rounds

Priya Raman Office manager, client accounts

Jonah Whitfield Indexing lead

Elena Sousa Aisle supervisor

Kenji Abara Scanning desk

Office and the round

Mara Okonkwo, founder, operations. She founded the archive in 2004 and runs day-to-day operations at Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport. Tomas Lindqvist, driver, collection rounds.

He drives the Tuesday and Thursday pickups and unloads at the dock, where barcodes are checked before a box is accepted into the aisle. Priya Raman, office manager, client accounts. She keeps client accounts, monthly invoices, and booking requests that come in by phone on +00 20 7000 1404 or by email at hello@shoko-archives.example.

Between them they cover the office side of a collection: who is coming, which round, and how the visit will be invoiced at €45 for up to 40 boxes.

Index, aisle, and scanning desk

Jonah Whitfield, indexing lead. He is responsible for the barcode label and for the aisle, bay, and shelf address on every box. Elena Sousa, aisle supervisor.

She supervises the 14 aisles and the 38,000-box capacity of the store, and she knows where a box sits once it is shelved. Kenji Abara, scanning desk. He runs scan on demand when you need a page from a box that should stay in the aisle, including drawings for the architects' studio and its 140 boxes.

Ask for a file by box number. A standard return is the next working day, at €6 per box, or the same day at €18 if you call before 11:00.

How to reach them

The office is open Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00. Saturday, 08:00–12:00, is retrievals only, and the unit is closed on Sunday. The next pickup round is Tuesday.

For a new collection, use the booking form or email hello@shoko-archives.example. For a box already in the aisle, quote the box number and ask for a next-working-day retrieval or, before 11:00, a same-day retrieval. Destruction, when you want it, is requested from the same office and comes with a certificate at €2.20 per box.

The six names above are the people who do the work. The phone for all of them is +00 20 7000 1404.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

How we handle what you send us.

This note says what we do with the details you send when you book a collection or join the Hall Two waitlist. It is written for clients of Shoko Archives at Unit 7, Lindenport.

What you send us

The booking form asks for your name, company, email, phone, box count, preferred round, a message, and consent. Box count is 1–40, 41–120, or 120+. Preferred round is Tuesday or Thursday.

The Hall Two waitlist asks for an email, sent to hello@shoko-archives.example. You may also call +00 20 7000 1404 or write to that same address. We use booking details to arrange a collection, to index boxes to your account, and to invoice monthly.

We use a waitlist email to write about Hall Two opening in spring. Priya Raman holds client accounts. We do not sell these details.

Boxes and the paper inside them

The paper inside a box belongs to you. We index the box number and the aisle, bay, and shelf. We do not read the contents unless you ask for a scan on demand or a retrieval that requires the file to be handled at the desk.

Kenji Abara scans only what you ask for. A legal hold stays sealed until you tell us it has ended. Secure destruction with a certificate, at €2.20 per box, happens only on your request.

We keep account and booking details while you have boxes in the 14 aisles, or while a waitlist request is open. When no box of yours remains and you want the account details removed, write to hello@shoko-archives.example.

Who to ask

Questions about this note go to hello@shoko-archives.example or +00 20 7000 1404. The office is open Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00. Saturday, 08:00–12:00, is for retrievals only.

Sunday is closed. The address is Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport. Mara Okonkwo is responsible for operations.

This page does not set a storage price or a retrieval time; those sit on the price list and the indexing page. Consent on the booking form means we may use the details to answer that request. If you use Email us to book instead of the form, sending the message is the same kind of request.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
Terms

The basics of the service.

These terms cover collection, storage, retrieval, and destruction at Shoko Archives, Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport. The published price list and the published hours are part of them.

The service

You book a collection. We collect on Tuesday or Thursday, barcode each standard box, index it to an aisle, bay, and shelf, and shelve it. You request a box by number.

We return it the next working day, or the same day if you request that before 11:00. We take invoices and ledgers, HR files, contracts, project drawings, legal holds, and closed-year boxes. We do not take loose unboxed paper as a standing load, and we do not take stock or personal belongings.

A legal hold is not destroyed while you still call it a hold. Destruction is only on your request and comes with a certificate. The facility is the 14 aisles at Unit 7, capacity 38,000 standard boxes, founded in 2004.

Prices and invoices

Prices are in euros and exclude VAT. Collection visit (up to 40 boxes): €45 per visit. Standard archive box with barcode: €3.50 each.

Storage: €0.42 per box per month. Retrieval, next working day: €6 per box. Urgent same-day retrieval: €18 per box.

Secure destruction with certificate: €2.20 per box. Invoicing is monthly. A booking form is a request until we confirm the round.

Counts of 41–120 or 120+ are split across Tuesday and Thursday rounds. Saturday, 08:00–12:00, is retrievals only. Monday to Friday the hours are 07:30–18:00.

Sunday is closed. The next pickup round is Tuesday. Phone +00 20 7000 1404.

Email hello@shoko-archives.example.

Your instructions

You decide when a box is stored and when it is destroyed. Quote the box number for a retrieval or a scan. Scan on demand is a request for a page, handled at the scanning desk by Kenji Abara, and the original stays in the aisle unless you ask for the box itself.

We follow the address on the barcode. Elena Sousa supervises the aisles. Hall Two, opening in spring, is a separate waitlist and is not part of a current storage booking.

Joining that list does not reserve an aisle and does not change these prices. Operations sit with Mara Okonkwo. Client accounts and monthly invoices sit with Priya Raman.

pages.title: Thanks
pages.content:
Thanks

We have your message.

Your request has been sent from this page. A collection is not on a round until the office confirms Tuesday or Thursday. A waitlist note still has to reach hello@shoko-archives.example.

What we have

Thank you. If you sent the booking form, we have your request for a collection. If you joined the Hall Two waitlist from the form, we have your email.

If the waitlist path opened your email app, you still need to send the message: you are not on the list until it has gone to hello@shoko-archives.example. A booking becomes a round only when we confirm Tuesday or Thursday. Keep the box count you chose — 1–40, 41–120, or 120+ — in case we ask you to repeat it.

Priya Raman handles client accounts and matches a confirmed visit to the van. Tomas Lindqvist drives the round.

While you wait

Office hours are Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00. Saturday is 08:00–12:00 and is for retrievals only. Sunday is closed.

The phone is +00 20 7000 1404. The address is Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport. The next pickup round is Tuesday.

If your matter is a box already on the shelf, call and quote the box number rather than waiting on a new-collection reply. Next-working-day retrieval is €6 per box. Same-day retrieval is €18 per box when the request is in before 11:00.

For a new collection, the visit is €45 for up to 40 boxes, excluding VAT, and the standard box with barcode is €3.50.

A correction, if you need one

You do not need to send a second form for the same request. If the phone number or the preferred round is wrong, email hello@shoko-archives.example with the correction and your company name. We invoice monthly, after the work, against the published list.

Storage is €0.42 per box per month once a box is in the aisle. Secure destruction, if you later ask for it, is €2.20 per box with a certificate. Until indexing has given you a box number, there is nothing to retrieve.

Jonah Whitfield's team issues that number after the collection. Hall Two, if that is what you asked about, opens in spring.

posts.title: How long should a business keep its invoices?
posts.excerpt: We do not set the holding period for your invoices; you do, and a closed-year box in a numbered aisle is how that decision is carried out.
posts.content:
Offices ask how long an invoice should stay. Shoko Archives does not set that period. We store the box. The period belongs to the business, agreed with the people who already advise you on accounts. What we can describe, from the paper that arrives at Unit 7, is how a holding period is carried out once you have chosen it.

What belongs in a closed-year box

An invoice that is still in use belongs at the desk. An invoice from a closed year, which nobody opens in the working week, is a candidate for a closed-year box. We collect invoices and ledgers on the same rounds as HR files, contracts, project drawings, and legal holds. The box is a standard archive box with a barcode. It leaves your office on a Tuesday or Thursday collection, is indexed to an aisle, bay, and shelf, and sits in one of the 14 aisles at Unit 7, Harlow Mead Trading Estate, Lindenport, until you ask for it.

A family clinic keeps 90 boxes on a retention schedule. The schedule, not the shelf, decides which box is still in its holding period and which box may be destroyed. A six-partner law office keeps 220 boxes of closed matters. The reason for holding them is different, and the mechanics are the same. An architects' studio keeps 140 boxes of drawings and calls for a scan when one sheet is needed. Invoices follow the clinic's pattern. You name the rule. We keep the box at that address until your rule says it can go.

While the box is in holding

While the box is in holding, you can still get the paper. Request it by box number. A standard retrieval is the next working day and costs €6 per box, excluding VAT. If you need it the same day, ask before 11:00, and the urgent retrieval is €18 per box. If you need a page rather than the box, the scanning desk can scan on demand, and the box goes back to its aisle, bay, and shelf. Kenji Abara runs that desk. Saturday retrievals run from 08:00 to 12:00. The store is closed on Sunday. Weekday hours are Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:00.

Storage during the holding period is €0.42 per box per month. A collection visit is €45 and covers up to 40 boxes. The box itself is €3.50 with the barcode. Invoicing is monthly. None of these prices is a reason to keep a box longer than your schedule says, and none of them is a reason to destroy it early. They are the cost of the aisle while you wait out the period you set.

When the period ends

When the schedule says the invoices can go, ask for secure destruction. It is €2.20 per box and comes with a certificate. We do not destroy a box because a calendar has turned, or because a shelf looks full. The capacity of the store is 38,000 standard boxes, across Aisle 1–14, so fullness is not the prompt. Your instruction is the prompt. A legal hold is the clear case: if you tell us a box is under a hold, it stays sealed, even when the closed year on the spine looks old.

Keep it findable

Indexing is what makes the later choice possible. Jonah Whitfield leads it. Without a box number, a phrase such as the invoices from that closed year is only a description, and descriptions drift. With a barcode and an aisle–bay–shelf address, the same box can be retrieved the next working day, scanned, or destroyed with a certificate. Elena Sousa supervises the aisles where those addresses sit. Tomas Lindqvist collects on the Tuesday and Thursday rounds. Priya Raman keeps the client account the monthly invoice is sent to. Mara Okonkwo runs operations, and founded the archive in 2004.

If you are deciding this month what to do with a stack of invoices, split the stack. Keep at the desk anything the office still posts against or still disputes. Box the closed year. Book a Tuesday or Thursday round. The next pickup round is Tuesday. Send a count of 1–40, 41–120, or 120+. Phone +00 20 7000 1404 or email hello@shoko-archives.example. Write your own holding rule on the account. When that rule ends, write again and name the box number. The length of time is yours. The numbered aisle is the part we look after.
